entries.title: The Duchy of Narvea
entries.subtitle: Country Profile
entries.text: The Duchy of Narvea Country Profile A concise visual guide to the mapped Baltic country where the story takes place, including its cities, diplomatic legacy, divided authority, institutions, and multilingual culture. The Duchy of Narvea At a glance The Duchy of Narvea is the main country in which the story takes place. It is a large, sovereign Baltic state stretching along much of the eastern Baltic coast, from the approaches to St. Petersburg toward the frontier near Gdansk. Narvea is a constitutional duchy with two real centers of authority: the Ducal Crown and the parliamentary state . The Duke is an independent sovereign, not a subordinate noble. Parliament and the Prime Minister control ordinary government. Sovereignty resides jointly in the Crown and the Nation. Identity Narvean is a civic identity shared across a culturally varied population. Citizens may belong to different regional, linguistic, religious, urban, or rural communities while identifying fully and politically as Narvean. The country modernized without erasing its older institutions. Modern ministries, elections, police, and armed forces exist beside a ducal court, inherited ranks, ceremonial precedence, and a separate Ducal Guard. European diplomacy Narvea historically became a center of European diplomacy. Opposing powers gathered there to resolve disputes before they escalated into open conflict, giving the duchy influence far beyond its size or military strength. During the Napoleonic Wars of 1803 to 1815, Narvea played an important and constructive role in containing the continental crisis. The settlements of this period also began shaping the country's borders into their modern form. In 1917, negotiations held in Narvea contained an eastern political crisis before it could become a revolution. In 1939, another Narvean settlement stopped escalation between opposing powers and prevented a major continental war. These agreements allowed continental borders and political history to develop along a different course. That diplomatic legacy made multilingualism part of Narvean public culture. People in authority are expected to know several languages, but the custom is not limited to officials. Ordinary Narveans may switch languages during everyday conversation for precision, courtesy, emphasis, or habit, even when diplomacy is nowhere near the room. Bird's Nest, the city with many names Bird's Nest has an intentionally unusual name. Most negotiations between rival nations take place there, and every country uses a different title for the same city. Bird's Nest is the Narvean name for this shared diplomatic ground, reflecting a place where competing powers gather without fully belonging to one another. Territory Long Baltic coastline and several major ports Important agricultural regions and trade routes Multiple linguistic, religious, and cultural regions Strategic frontier with Russia Strong commercial and military importance in the Baltic Exact borders remain provisional until the alternate-history timeline is finalized. The two capitals Rennel Rennel, in the historic Narva region, is the seat of the Crown. It contains the Ducal Palace, court, Privy Council, Guard headquarters, dynastic archives, heraldic offices, and ceremonial institutions. It represents dynasty, continuity, military tradition, and the old state. Vilen Vilen is the parliamentary and administrative capital. It contains Parliament, the Prime Minister's office, ministries, major courts, central bureaucracy, and financial institutions. It represents law, administration, commerce, and modern political life. The Prime Minister travels to Rennel for formal audiences with the Duke. The Duke travels to Vilen for major constitutional ceremonies, including the opening of Parliament. Turon Turon is a significant city and the headquarters of MSF. MSF is a fully private intelligence business that sells its services to the government while retaining control of its own succession and internal affairs. A substantial part of its officer corps is concentrated in Turon, giving the company a degree of local power that quietly troubles the central government. If MSF ever chose open defiance, its presence in Turon could support a small rebellion or even an attempt at secession. Officer culture, divided logistics, constitutional loyalty, and the absence of any desire to rebel keep that capacity dormant. Politicians know that the final safeguard is officer decency, not an enforceable external restraint. Crown and State The Ducal Crown The Duke is head of state and constitutional guardian. He appoints the Prime Minister who holds parliamentary confidence, promulgates laws, receives ambassadors, grants honours, consults the Privy Council, commands the Ducal Guard, and may hold narrowly defined reserve powers. The parliamentary state The Prime Minister is head of government. Parliament, Cabinet, ministries, the civil service, courts, police, and national armed forces handle ordinary administration, taxation, defence policy, education, infrastructure, economic policy, and foreign policy. Neither side is decorative, and neither rules alone. Security institutions Narvean Armed Forces The national military is funded by the state and controlled through the constitutional government. It may include the Army, Navy, Air Force, reserves, territorial forces, and military intelligence. Ducal Guard The Ducal Guard belongs to the Crown. It protects the ducal family and residences, guards Crown institutions, performs ceremonial duties, and may have limited constitutional-security responsibilities. Narvean Police Ordinary policing belongs to the parliamentary state, most likely under the Ministry of the Interior. Palace security remains separate from public law enforcement. Councils and service rank The Privy Council advises the Duke on constitutional questions, foreign affairs, national security, appointments, dynastic matters, and emergencies. It does not replace Cabinet or Parliament. The Council of State bridges Crown and government through constitutional review, administrative law, senior appointments, disputes, and emergency continuity. Its unresolved jurisdiction becomes most important when ordinary constitutional sovereignty collides with hidden supernatural authority that the public state cannot formally acknowledge. Narvea retains its own hierarchy of court and civil ranks. Rank determines precedence and status, but does not necessarily describe a person's actual job. A State Councillor might serve as an ambassador, judge, governor, rector, or senior ministry official. Drake holds the rank of State Councillor and the office of Official for Special Assignments. He is an elite executive troubleshooter attached to a high-ranking personal office and is free from routine administration. He can carry delegated authority into confidential criminal investigations, political counter-espionage, emergency corruption audits, and diplomatic errands. His friendship with the Duke begins when Drake is the only official willing to tell him that he is wrong. That refusal to flatter earns exceptional access and occasional forgiveness, but later makes Drake deeply unpopular at Court, where courtiers deride him as the Duke's pampered favorite. Cultural character Narvea carries layered coastal, inland, courtly, mercantile, urban, rural, and frontier traditions. Catholic and Orthodox communities coexist across regions with distinct architecture, memory, dialect, and politics. The result is not a uniform cultural mixture. The state itself is what connects its different regions. The central tension Narvea lives through a permanent partnership, and occasional rivalry, between inherited continuity and popular government. A modern minister can hold an old civil rank. A national officer can attend a ceremony governed by ducal precedence. An elected Prime Minister controls policy but still travels to the palace for a formal audience. That tension between modern public life and inherited hierarchy is central to the country, and to the story unfolding inside it. Narvean State Archive

entries.title: What Can You Tell Me About Magi?
entries.subtitle: Magistry
entries.text: What Can You Tell Me About Magi? Magistry A dialogue on the nature, secrecy, religion, and politics of Magi. What Can You Tell Me About Magi? Journalist: “What can you tell me about Magi?” Fionn: “That depends on whether you want the answer fit for a child, a priest, or a judge.” Journalist: “The true one.” Fionn: “A dangerous preference.” Fionn: “Very well. Magi do not create miracles. They exploit them.” Journalist: “Explain.” Fionn: “Nature is full of pressure points. Fault lines. Small mercies in the machinery. Most men live their entire lives without seeing them. A Magus sees them, presses where others only endure, and obtains from the world an effect that the world was already willing to permit.” Journalist: “So your craft is natural.” Fionn: “Do not say that too loudly. It upsets both the devout and the educated, though for different reasons.” Journalist: “And the common word for it?” Fionn: “Magic. Superstition. Blasphemy. Treason, on difficult days.” Journalist: “You speak of it with very little reverence.” Fionn: “I was not asked to admire it.” Journalist: “Then what are Magi, truly?” Fionn: “Loopholes. Human ones.” Journalist: “You say that as if it were an accusation.” Fionn: “It often is.” Journalist: “And what follows from this?” Fionn: “What follows is secrecy. Always secrecy. A society can forgive murder more easily than it can forgive a wound in its understanding of nature.” Journalist: “That is a severe claim.” Fionn: “It is also a practical one.” Journalist: “You mean that a witness must die.” Fionn: “I mean that the world protects its coherence with astonishing cruelty.” Journalist: “That was not my question.” Fionn: “No. But it was the truthful answer.” Journalist: “And the Church?” Fionn: “The Church is wiser than statesmen and less honest than philosophers. It knows enough to fear us, enough to use us, and enough to deny both.” Journalist: “And politics?” Fionn: “Politics is forbidden.” Journalist: “Forbidden, or impossible?” Fionn: “Neither. Merely expensive.” Journalist,Fionn

entries.title: The Drowned Choir
entries.subtitle: HI-003 · Operational encounter
entries.text: The Drowned Choir HI-003 · Operational encounter HI-003 the-drowned-choir The Drowned Choir Operational encounter embodied environmental A pale girl rises from the river with her eyes sewn shut by fishing line and a dress made from dead fish. She enslaves the souls of people drowned in the river and uses their hands to pull new victims beneath the surface. Maren and the surviving officers report trained swimmers being pulled down by an unexpected force. Darkness, panic, dangerous current, exhaustion, and mutually reinforced testimony remain the available material explanations, while the empty contraband boats provide no visible attacker. The girl is an embodied Holumn controlling the river's accumulated drowned souls. The dead reach through the water as her hands and speak through her as the Drowned Choir. Submerged hands seize swimmers by the legs and pull downward. Lynleit's blue flame burns them even beneath the water and forces their grip open. They cannot pass through the surface layer beneath her feet once her water walking manifests. The girl's tilted head reads as confusion when Lynleit remains above the river. The drowned hands can be injured by blue flame beneath the water and cannot reach through the river's surface. These limits let Lynleit escape their grasp, but no method of freeing the enslaved dead or defeating the girl is confirmed. The Drowned Choir takes the crews of contraband boats before they reach the bridge, allowing real criminal traffic to continue without living operators. The encounter establishes that a Holumn can absorb human wrongdoing into its own pattern and make an ordinary conspiracy appear supernaturally self-moving. embodied,environmental

entries.title: The Last Piece
entries.subtitle: HI-002 · Missing-person incident
entries.text: The Last Piece HI-002 · Missing-person incident HI-002 the-last-piece The Last Piece Missing-person incident event curse A puzzle purchased at a market compels its owner to finish it. When the final piece is placed, the owner disappears and enters the missing-persons archive. Investigators see a purchased object, a developed obsession, and a disappearance. The puzzle may be treated as an unrelated possession, a clue to voluntary flight, or an instrument used by another person. The compulsion and completion belong to the same rule. Placing the final piece completes the condition that permits the disappearance. Attention narrows into addiction. Completion is followed by permanent disappearance, while the object remains available to be found again. No countermeasure is confirmed. Refusing completion appears safer than solving the object, but the strength and transfer of the compulsion remain unknown. The incident establishes that a Holumn may be an event encoded into an ordinary object, with no creature concealed inside it. event,curse

entries.title: The Nameless Street
entries.subtitle: HI-005 · Urban legend and direct encounter
entries.text: The Nameless Street HI-005 · Urban legend and direct encounter HI-005 the-nameless-street The Nameless Street Urban legend and direct encounter environmental event curse A lost visitor may enter a deserted old street whose lanes, stairs, courtyards, and hills cannot be reconciled with the surrounding city. Following anyone encountered there may prevent the visitor from returning to ordinary streets. Felix sees Lynleit stop responding, move toward a city bench, and faint after lunch. Dizziness, a severe headache, a dream, or a neurological episode can explain the only part of the incident another person directly observes. The street behaves as a place-bound Holumn whose body is an impossible route and whose rule uses isolation, pursuit, and a fatal fall. Whether the girl, the boy, and the red balloon belong permanently to that rule remains unknown. The visitor is separated without perceiving a threshold, becomes dizzy and disoriented, and cannot navigate the district by ordinary geometry. Lynleit follows a crying girl to a broken fence, is pushed toward a dead boy below, and returns to a city bench before impact. The urban warning instructs visitors not to follow anyone encountered on the street. It is not known whether refusing the lure guarantees escape or why Lynleit returns after following it. The encounter establishes that a Holumn can occupy urban arrangement itself. Its later connection to Fionn's fall may be anticipation, memory, coincidence, or a rule that makes one death resemble another; the evidence does not yet distinguish them. environmental,event,curse

entries.title: The River That Is Too Deep
entries.subtitle: HI-004 · Accumulated incident pattern
entries.text: The River That Is Too Deep HI-004 · Accumulated incident pattern HI-004 the-river-that-is-too-deep The River That Is Too Deep Accumulated incident pattern embodied environmental Something immense moves beneath the city river despite stretches too shallow to contain it. Impossible waves damage boats and kayaks, while drowned bodies lose pieces to bites larger than any expected river predator could make. Each report can be separated into wake damage, submerged debris, boating accidents, postmortem animal activity, or exaggerated witness comparison. Together they remain difficult to explain without inventing a cause the river should not contain. The leviathan may be an animal-like Holumn, the river giving itself predatory mass, or a depth that exists only when the manifestation passes through it. The river behaves as though it can briefly contain a body larger than its physical depth. Water displacement, impact damage, and feeding traces persist after the shape itself is gone. No countermeasure is confirmed. Its dependence on the river may be a boundary, but it is not yet known whether the water contains the Holumn or belongs to it. The pattern supports the possibility that the Spill changes a place's physical capacity as well as the creatures that can enter it. embodied,environmental

entries.title: The Voice on the Line
entries.subtitle: HI-001 · Victim testimony
entries.text: The Voice on the Line HI-001 · Victim testimony HI-001 the-voice-on-the-line The Voice on the Line Victim testimony disembodied curse Have you heard of a telephone call that answers to you in your own voice? At first I thought whoever was on the phone was repeating me. But it was my own voice. At first it felt like an echo, as all it did was repeat my words. But then it started calling me incessantly, and it was talking to me, in bizarre ways. In my own voice. Police and communications specialists would first investigate harassment, recording fraud, a compromised exchange, equipment failure, or a witness in psychological distress. Magi and special envoys treat the change from repetition to unsolicited speech as the decisive detail. Something learned the witness's voice, then began using it without the witness. Imitation develops into initiative. The calls become incessant and the borrowed voice speaks in ways the witness does not recognize as their own thought. No countermeasure is confirmed. The incident establishes that a Holumn can enter ordinary infrastructure and acquire presence without forming a visible body. disembodied,curse

entries.title: A Meeting Beyond Authority
entries.subtitle: MOM-005 · Unknowing Convergence
entries.text: A Meeting Beyond Authority MOM-005 · Unknowing Convergence At night on a hill overlooking Vilen, Sherie leads an illegal negotiation in which Drake seeks limited access to MSF resources without surrendering sensitive evidence. Binds the government and MSF investigations together through an alliance that is politically dangerous before anyone understands that the underlying threat is magical. It is Sherie's first independent diplomatic success, not a transfer of Drake's wider role as the story's primary strategic mind. A hill overlooking Vilen Sherie believes her uncle when the Court does not. Sherie is Drake's niece and is training under him to become a diplomat. The approach to Lynleit is entirely Sherie's idea and strategy. Sherie develops the plan against Drake's wishes, persuades him to participate, and takes charge of the meeting and negotiations. Drake remains opposed to the illegal approach but attends after Sherie overcomes his resistance. After the negotiation succeeds, Sherie asks Drake to praise and pamper her for her first achievement. Drake still cannot decide whether an alliance with Lynleit is a strategic advantage or a dangerous mistake. Drake remains the story's main strategic mind before and after this event. The meeting takes place at night on a hill overlooking Vilen. Drake does not hand sensitive evidence to people outside the aristocratic circle. He and Sherie request access to selected MSF resources and capabilities in exchange for concessions or favors. Sherie and Drake bring Heyk as their bodyguard and confidant. Lynleit brings Felix, Reiner, and Kyrien as her bodyguards and confidants. The main negotiation belongs to Lynleit, Sherie, and a reluctant Drake, while the others contribute opinions and warnings. Lynleit regards the request as dangerous. Felix openly protests, while Kyrien stays silent and tests the suspected conspiracy against his own past grievances. What concessions or favors do Drake and Sherie offer for the confirmed river-surveillance operation? What access or resources does Lynleit refuse beyond the limited operation? What would finally convince Drake that the alliance should be preserved or abandoned? Sherie must persuade Drake that Lynleit is worth the legal and political danger of contact. Sherie claims praise and pampering for her success while Drake remains uncertain about what she has created. The private agreement then produces a narrow intelligence operation. The team may inspect the suspected shipment but cannot arrest anyone or seize material. Drake drake Sherie sherie Lynleit lynleit Felix felix Reiner reiner Kyrien kyrien Heyk heyk

entries.title: After the Failed Attempt
entries.subtitle: MOM-001 · The Hidden Wager
entries.text: After the Failed Attempt MOM-001 · The Hidden Wager Lynleit interrogates Kyrien after his failed attempt to assassinate a Magus politician, then converts his prison risk into a secret recruitment. Creates the coercive bargain that begins Kyrien's hidden association with MSF in the first few chapters. Lynleit accepts the risk because she senses danger approaching before she can prove its shape. The decision also leaves a surviving Magus politician whose later retaliation reaches her. Police office Kyrien has made a failed attempt to assassinate a politician who belongs to the Magi world. The immediate aftermath brings him into a police office. Lynleit conducts the interrogation. Lynleit invokes an extraordinary transfer clause in MSF's government service contract, drafted under Fionn for extraordinary threats. The transfer gives her control of Kyrien's case, and she does not disclose the secret recruitment to Fionn. Kyrien faces prison unless he agrees to become Lynleit's secret helper. His freedom remains conditional on accepting Lynleit's demands, leaving him confined to her whims. Lynleit's private strategy is to keep Kyrien as a secret trump card against Helena. The recruitment occurs within the first few chapters, well before Fionn's assassination. Lynleit acts because her intuition warns her of near-future danger before she has enough evidence to define it. Lynleit is Fionn's biological daughter. Helena is Lynleit's stepmother and Fionn's wife. Lynleit already suspects Helena of being an enemy despite that family relationship. Kyrien's father held an important position in Narvea's military. The targeted politician was involved in causing his father's death. Kyrien obtained the knowledge and tools for the attempt through his father's military background. The attempt fails solely because the politician belongs to the Magi world. The politician's survival later creates consequences for Lynleit. Lynleit notices Helena probing Fionn's schedules, visitors to the family house, trusted officers, and Lynleit's own travel. Lynleit suspects murder because Helena appears to be studying the family too carefully. What is the politician's name, office, and exact role in Kyrien's father's death? How does the surviving politician later retaliate against Lynleit? What initial cover story conceals Kyrien's release and unofficial MSF association? Kyrien's father's death, the politician's involvement, and the military knowledge behind the attempt still need connective scenes. Kyrien enters Lynleit's service unwillingly. Lynleit must later decide who, if anyone, can be trusted with the secret. The arrangement preserves him as hidden leverage against Helena through the early investigation. Fionn's much later assassination vindicates Lynleit's warning without proving that she understood its source. Lynleit lynleit Kyrien kyrien

entries.title: Ash in the Family House
entries.subtitle: MOM-002 · Vanishing Point
entries.text: Ash in the Family House MOM-002 · Vanishing Point Before the crisis reaches her home directly, Lynleit clumsily chases a grey male cat named Ash, catches him, then cannot bring herself to expel him into the rain. Shows Lynleit's clumsy and childish private side while using the grey intruder as an omen. Outside threats and tragedies have begun to bleed into her life, and the escaping cat becomes an emotional symbol for her slipping leads, understanding, and sense of safety. The Director's House The scene occurs in the early chapters, after danger has begun outside but before Lynleit's life starts to collapse. The grey cat is male and is named Ash. Ash's trespass and permanent stay allow the reader to treat him as an omen of outside threats entering Lynleit's private life without any character naming him as one. inferred The family maintained an original house in Turon while Lynleit's mother was alive and Lynleit was in junior school. After her mother's death, the family moved to a Vilen residence for Fionn's access to the capital. Lynleit accepted the move only after securing the third-floor study-bedroom. The Vilen house is a three-floor family residence on a wooded hill above the river that flows toward the city center, with a small rear park and garden. Lynleit values the thick vegetation and the sound of leaves and branches in the wind. She regards nearby flowing water as life energy and seeks its emotional grounding despite her childhood fear of drowning. The garden-facing first floor contains glass-enclosed relaxation areas that preserve contact with nature through every season. Lynleit personally chases Ash through the house, revealing a clumsier and more childish side of her than her public role usually permits. The chase can imply that Ash's repeated escapes echo Lynleit's fear that her leads, understanding, and safety are also escaping her control. inferred Lynleit eventually catches Ash. She cannot bring herself to expel him because rain is falling outside. Ash decides to remain and becomes a permanent loiterer in the family home. Who else in the household accepts or resists Ash's permanent presence? The first disappearances have begun outside Lynleit's private life, but the full crisis, Fionn's death, and the destruction of her family security remain ahead. Ash remains inside the house as a quiet domestic echo of the danger Lynleit cannot keep outside. Later losses can turn the once-comic chase into an omen whose meaning becomes clear only in retrospect. Lynleit lynleit Ash ash

entries.title: At the End of the First Arc
entries.subtitle: MOM-012 · Lynleit Disappears
entries.text: At the End of the First Arc MOM-012 · Lynleit Disappears After a story-long accumulation of functional trust and non-sexual intimacy, Lynleit and Kyrien finally have sex at the end of the first arc, shortly before her pregnancy and disappearance. Completes a progression that begins with protected knowledge and shared warmth after the river incident, deepens through emotional refuge after Fionn's murder, and becomes sexual only when the first arc is closing. Unspecified location Lynleit and Kyrien's intimacy develops slowly and functionally across the entire story. The relationship remains non-sexual through the river aftermath and the much later hotel-room refuge. Their relationship becomes sexual at the end of the first arc. The encounter occurs before Lynleit's pregnancy and disappearance. What final circumstances bring them together at the end of the arc? Is this encounter the conception of their son? When does Lynleit realize she is pregnant, and how much time passes before she disappears? The river incident establishes silent physical trust. The hotel-room refuge after Fionn's murder establishes emotional safety. Further acts of practical care build the intimacy that precedes their final threshold. Lynleit becomes pregnant close to the end of the arc and disappears to keep the child beyond the conflict's reach. Kyrien is left to direct MSF without knowing that she carries their son. Lynleit lynleit Kyrien kyrien

entries.title: Beyond the Cordon
entries.subtitle: MOM-010 · The Quarantine
entries.text: Beyond the Cordon MOM-010 · The Quarantine Hiyu enters the quarantined park to test his impossible suspicion that magic is involved in the disappearances. Yulia goes with him to prove the theory wrong and keep him alive. Places two opposite investigative methods inside the same impossible case: Hiyu's generative intuition reaches the right category without understanding it, while Yulia's disciplined criminology loses the ordinary rules it depends upon. The quarantined park in Vilen Hiyu and Yulia are university students in their mid-twenties who study criminology. Yulia is a classical ISTJ and the top student in their class, with meticulous command of detail and criminological protocol. Hiyu is an ENTP whose personal investigations rely on intuitive threads, improvised methods, and rapid hypothesis generation. Without knowing that magic exists, Hiyu suspects it is involved in the disappearances. Yulia enters partly to prove him wrong and partly to prevent him from facing the danger alone. How do they bypass the cordon? What do they find, and how do they survive or escape? What lasting evidence, injury, or change in their relationship follows the trespass? The widening disappearance case gives Hiyu enough fragments to form an impossible but directionally correct theory. Yulia rejects the conclusion but refuses to let him test it alone. Their evidence connects two civilian students to the larger institutional response. Hiyu correctly suspects magic but still lacks any complete knowledge of it. Hiyu hiyu Yulia yulia

entries.title: Father Mikhail Discovers the Breach
entries.subtitle: MOM-015 · Divided Attention
entries.text: Father Mikhail Discovers the Breach MOM-015 · Divided Attention Father Mikhail becomes the first authority to discover that Lynleit has shared forbidden knowledge of magic with outsiders. Kyrien corrects her attempt to limit the breach to himself by revealing that Felix and Reiner also know. Turns a private breach into pressure for an institutional answer. Lynleit's promise to handle the witnesses on her own terms becomes an early cause of MSF's later conversion from a purely private intelligence company into a partly Magi enterprise accountable to the Magiarchy and the Church. Unspecified private location Father Mikhail is the first authority to learn that Lynleit has disclosed forbidden knowledge of magic to outsiders. Lynleit is unprepared for the discovery and promises to resolve the exposure on her own terms. Mikhail asks whether Kyrien is the only witness, and Lynleit reassures him. Kyrien immediately states that Felix and Reiner also know. Mikhail responds by looking at Lynleit in judgment rather than escalating the confrontation openly. Lynleit again promises to handle the problem in her own way. Mikhail leaves her with the warning: 'What you do is none of my business, but don't be surprised if I'll be sent to clean up your mess.' The encounter becomes an early cause of MSF's later transformation into a partly Magi private enterprise reporting to the Magiarchy and the Church. Kyrien gives no reason for correcting Lynleit, leaving the reader to infer whether literal honesty, distrust of institutional half-truths, or another motive drives him. inferred Mikhail does not define his authority. His restraint and final warning imply that the Church may later send him back with powers he is not claiming in this conversation. inferred Where does the confrontation occur, and what evidence prevents Lynleit from denying the original disclosure? What action does Lynleit mean by handling the problem in her own way? What narrow authority would allow Mikhail to be sent back to clean up the breach? What formal agreement later makes MSF accountable to both the Magiarchy and the Church while preserving its private ownership? Lynleit has already allowed Kyrien, Felix, and Reiner to operate with knowledge that ordinary MSF officers and outsiders are forbidden to possess. Lynleit must create an institutional place for people she refuses to suppress or surrender. The eventual answer changes MSF's mandate and places part of the private company inside the Magiarchal and Church order. Lynleit lynleit Kyrien kyrien Felix felix Reiner reiner Father Mikhail father-mikhail

entries.title: Shelter after the Accusation
entries.subtitle: MOM-011 · Clear Her Name
entries.text: Shelter after the Accusation MOM-011 · Clear Her Name After exhausting her available resources to escape the directed hunt for her arrest, Lynleit reaches Kyrien's hotel-room hideout and finally loses the composure that carried her through the immediate crisis. Marks a much later threshold in an intimacy that began functionally after the river incident. Safety, grief, and care turn the coerced alliance into emotional reliance without making the relationship sexual yet. Kyrien's hotel-room hideout Lynleit acts rationally and efficiently during the accusation and escape. Helena's response is a directed hunt for Lynleit's arrest. Lynleit uses every available resource she can reach to evade capture. Her emotions surface only after she reaches safety in Kyrien's hotel room. She stays the night. There is no sexual interaction between them. Kyrien holds her while she falls asleep. The hotel-room refuge occurs much later than the river incident and only after Fionn has been murdered. Their earlier intimate encounters are non-sexual and arise functionally from isolation, danger, cold, near drowning, or emotional rupture. The first trigger is Kyrien's silent protection of Lynleit's water-walking secret and their back-to-back attempt to share body heat after the river incident. Later sexual intimacy is not deliberately pursued. It develops as something emotionally unavoidable. Their relationship becomes sexual at the end of the first arc. The sexual encounter precedes Lynleit's pregnancy and disappearance. How does Lynleit locate the hideout without leading pursuit to Kyrien? What does she say once her composure breaks? What changes between them the following morning? Helena has used Fionn's death to frame Lynleit and direct a hunt for her arrest, forcing her to rely on the secret ally she recruited long before the danger became visible. Their bond remains non-sexual at this point, but it becomes a private source of safety that later intimacy can grow from without feeling sudden or sought for its own sake. Kyrien next helps Lynleit establish contact with Felix and Reiner, beginning her slow campaign to reclaim MSF while she remains hunted. Lynleit lynleit Kyrien kyrien

entries.title: The Coat Fionn Left Behind
entries.subtitle: MOM-016 · Clear Her Name
entries.text: The Coat Fionn Left Behind MOM-016 · Clear Her Name Long after losing a blue suede jacket in the river, Lynleit learns that Fionn had discreetly replaced the blue coat she wears with a garment sewn from material called the hide of leviathan. Turns a familiar piece of clothing into evidence of Fionn's concealed care. Its protection is useful but conditional, and its autonomous changes of form keep the inheritance from behaving like a passive suit of armour. Unspecified Lynleit loses a fitted blue suede jacket during the Drowned Choir attack and later complains about the loss because she liked it. After Fionn's death, Lynleit discovers that he had discreetly replaced the blue coat she wears. The replacement is sewn from material called the hide of leviathan. The coat can shield its user from minor magically induced damage and phenomena. Wearing the coat is not enough to activate its protection. Lynleit must cover the threatened part of her body or remove the garment and place or throw it over someone who needs protection. The coat chooses its own form. It may appear as a coat, scarf, an imitation of Lynleit's lost blue jacket, or another piece of clothing. Lynleit cannot command the change, which creates occasional practical and comic problems. When did Fionn replace the original coat, and how did he do it without Lynleit noticing? How does Lynleit discover the substitution after his death? What does hide of leviathan mean, and is it connected to the river phenomenon recorded as HI-004? What counts as minor magically induced damage, and what limits the coat's protection? Why does the coat choose forms autonomously, and can it refuse the form Lynleit needs? Lynleit loses the blue suede jacket during the river operation. Fionn dies without explaining the protective garment he had placed in her wardrobe. The inherited coat becomes part of Lynleit's equipment. Its changing forms can preserve the silhouette of the lost jacket, but its protection remains deliberate rather than automatic. Lynleit lynleit Fionn fionn

entries.title: The Empty Boats Beneath the Bridge
entries.subtitle: MOM-006 · Unknowing Convergence
entries.text: The Empty Boats Beneath the Bridge MOM-006 · Unknowing Convergence A covert MSF team descends from a bridge to inspect small night shipments requested by Drake and Sherie. The tarp-covered wooden boats arrive empty, the Drowned Choir attacks from below, and Kyrien secretly witnesses Lynleit burn the drowned hands and stand on the river. Carries an operation framed as contraband surveillance into the supernatural without a formal reveal, turns Lynleit's drowning fear into uncontrolled blue flame and forbidden water walking, and gives Kyrien a secret he chooses to protect before either character trusts the other openly. A Vilen river bridge linking a city street to the quarantined park Sherie and Drake ask Lynleit to assemble a loyal MSF team and investigate recurring night traffic on the Vilen river. Drake's intelligence identifies small boats moving only on the darkest nights. No operator is visible, the pattern appears intricate, and contraband remains a plausible explanation. The chosen bridge links a city street to the quarantined park. The plan requires Felix to freeze the bridge's civil safety cameras, maintain communications, and remain on the city side as fallback while the river team descends by rope, inspects the boats, and leaves by rope at the next bridge. Several nights produce no boats. Each unsuccessful watch consumes the limited camera window and exposes Lynleit or Kyrien to small oddities emerging from the quarantined park that the mission gives them no freedom to pursue. The successful interception occurs on the fifth watch. The unsuccessful watches reveal a branch breaking before the wind reaches the trees and a pale interruption in a frozen camera feed. The boats are small wooden craft with dark tarps over shallow holds. Fixed rudders keep them aligned while the current provides most of their movement. When the boats finally appear, Reiner, Lynleit, Kyrien, Maren, and Ivo descend and find them empty. Felix remains ashore. The empty boats, drowned hands, and pale girl imply that the Drowned Choir took the contraband crews before the interception, although the surviving officers cannot prove that connection. inferred The river attack begins while the officers search the empty boats for another explanation. The officers are capable swimmers. Reaching shore becomes difficult because unseen hands seize their legs and pull downward. After reaching land, Maren describes the sensation of hands gripping and pulling her legs. Reiner, Maren, and Ivo reach the street-facing city bank with Felix's fallback line without understanding what attacked them. They do not realize that Lynleit remains behind. The dead hands, the pale girl's drowned voices, and the pattern of new victims imply that she has bound people who drowned in the river across generations and uses them to pull others under. inferred Only Lynleit sees the hands clearly. They seize her most violently and drag her underwater. Lynleit wears a fitted blue suede jacket for the operation because it interferes less with ropes and wet timber than her usual coat. The hands tear the blue suede jacket away during the underwater struggle. The attack activates her childhood fear of drowning. Fury releases her blue flame at unsafe volume, and the fire catches and burns the drowned hands even beneath the water. After breaking the surface, Lynleit's palm meets resistance. She brings a knee and then both boots onto the same yielding layer until she stands above the river. The drowned hands reach upward from the darkness but cannot pass through the surface layer beneath Lynleit's feet. A pale girl emerges wearing a dress made from dead fish. Fishing line sews her eyes shut. The girl's silence and tilted head imply that a person standing on water contradicts the rule by which she takes victims. inferred Kyrien is present as Lynleit's concealed unofficial asset rather than an acknowledged MSF officer. The force in the river separates Kyrien from the official team and drives him toward the quarantined park side of the river. Kyrien reaches the park bank, enters the trees, and observes Lynleit's confrontation on the river from inside the quarantine. Only Kyrien witnesses Lynleit walking on water. Lynleit tests each step across the yielding surface and backs toward the park bank while the girl remains still. Kyrien is too careful to acknowledge what he saw and feigns innocence convincingly. Lynleit reaches the park side of the river without the jacket, where Kyrien is waiting among the trees. They remain inside the night park, drenched and struggling to catch their breath. They sit with their backs pressed together to share body heat while they recover. Lynleit indirectly asks whether Kyrien saw anything strange during the escape. Kyrien denies seeing anything, and his careful performance of innocence gives Lynleit nothing she can safely test. Kyrien's decision to protect the secret, made without an order from Lynleit, implies the first voluntary trust inside their coerced alliance. inferred What form does the river's scar take, and in what sense does the place remember the encounter? What intelligence survives the failed operation beyond the officers' separate accounts? Does the submerged blue flame leave a lasting injury on the Drowned Choir or only force the hands to release Lynleit? The hilltop agreement gives Drake and Sherie access to a small loyal MSF team without granting them control of the agency. Their first request is a limited investigation of apparently unmanned river shipments, with contraband still the leading material explanation. Felix, Reiner, Maren, and Ivo carry an account of impossible resistance from the city bank but no shared sight of its cause. Kyrien observes the river from the quarantined trees, and Lynleit later joins him on the park bank without the blue suede jacket. Drenched and seated back to back inside the park, they preserve a mutual silence around what he witnessed. Lynleit later complains about the lost jacket. Much later, after Fionn's murder, the hotel-room refuge deepens that physical trust into emotional reliance. Sherie sherie Drake drake Lynleit lynleit Felix felix Reiner reiner Kyrien kyrien

entries.title: The First Lines Back into MSF
entries.subtitle: MOM-013 · Clear Her Name
entries.text: The First Lines Back into MSF MOM-013 · Clear Her Name While Lynleit remains the target of an active arrest hunt, Kyrien helps her find secure ways to contact Felix and Reiner. Their reconnection becomes the first step in her slow campaign to reclaim MSF from Helena. Bridges Lynleit's immediate escape and hotel refuge to an organized counteroffensive. The hidden ally Helena did not know becomes the route back to the two trusted officers she does know. Unspecified secure contact points Lynleit remains actively hunted for arrest after escaping the immediate accusation. Kyrien helps her find ways to contact Felix and Reiner without surrendering her location. Felix and Reiner are the first trusted MSF officers brought back into her fugitive network. The renewed contact begins Lynleit's slow effort to reclaim MSF from Helena. The counteroffensive develops while Lynleit remains hunted. What secure method does Kyrien use to reach Felix and Reiner? Which officer responds first, and how does Lynleit prove the contact is genuine? What first foothold inside MSF can Felix and Reiner give her without exposing themselves? Which arresting authorities and MSF units are actively searching for Lynleit at this point? Lynleit reaches Kyrien's hotel room after exhausting her immediate escape resources, and his refuge becomes the only stable point in her flight. The four-person link gives Lynleit an internal line into Helena's MSF and begins a prolonged contest for legitimacy, intelligence, and control under the pressure of an active manhunt. Lynleit lynleit Kyrien kyrien Felix felix Reiner reiner

entries.title: The First Missing Man
entries.subtitle: MOM-003 · Vanishing Point
entries.text: The First Missing Man MOM-003 · Vanishing Point The first man to disappear appears to be the Spill's first victim, but he independently causes the crisis. His identity and significance remain concealed for most of the story while hidden factions begin exploiting the catastrophe he created. Makes the apparent first victim the buried cause of an independent crisis, allowing a later identity revelation to reframe both the Holumn disappearances and the agendas built around them. Vilen park, exact site unspecified The first missing person is a man. He is the person who causes the Spill. His identity and significance are not revealed for most of the story. He initially appears to be a victim. His role in causing the crisis remains concealed. The Spill begins independently of the hidden conspiracy and is later exploited by other actors. Other factions recognize and exploit the crisis for their own purposes. The later disappearances are caused by Holumns. Who is the man? How does he cause the Spill? Why does his identity become pivotal later? Which faction first recognizes and exploits what he caused? Who notices his disappearance first? His public identity and ordinary routine must conceal the significance he will acquire later. Holumns begin taking further victims. Investigators treat the first disappearance as the start of the case and do not know that the missing man caused the crisis.

entries.title: The Last Man out of the Park
entries.subtitle: MOM-009 · The Quarantine
entries.text: The Last Man out of the Park MOM-009 · The Quarantine A specially equipped paramilitary unit enters the sealed park and is massacred by forces it cannot understand. Captain Heyk becomes the sole survivor. Turns a public missing-person crisis into a state-level containment failure and gives Heyk the grief, access, and personal motive that carry him into Drake and Sherie's service. The quarantined park in Vilen The park quarantine follows the disappearances of citizens, private investigators, and police officers. Police enforce the first closure before the park is sealed even from them. The government deploys specially equipped paramilitary units to investigate the whole park. The unit commanded by Captain Heyk is massacred by forces he cannot understand or explain. Heyk is the sole survivor. The Ducal Guard evacuates him briefly under Drake's orders. He is subsequently recruited into the Ducal Guard as a field agent and bodyguard serving Drake and Sherie's interests. His continuing motive is grief for the squad he lost. What does Heyk perceive during the massacre, and which parts of his account can he articulate? Why does Drake have enough warning or access to order the Ducal Guard evacuation? What evidence, equipment, or injury leaves the park with Heyk? The public already knows that people are missing. Gas, poison, or another harmful substance remains a possible explanation, although no bodies have been recovered. Heyk enters Drake and Sherie's orbit carrying grief, survivor knowledge, and direct experience that no official material explanation can fully contain. Heyk heyk Drake drake Sherie sherie

entries.title: The Nameless Street
entries.subtitle: MOM-014 · Divided Attention
entries.text: The Nameless Street MOM-014 · Divided Attention During a casual walk after lunch with Felix, Lynleit enters a deserted labyrinthine street, follows a crying girl with a red balloon, sees a dead boy below a broken fence, and is pushed from the same ledge before waking on an ordinary city bench. Gives Lynleit a private memory of a child's fatal fall that later overwhelms her when she sees Fionn below the hill at the family house. Helena can use Lynleit's genuine shock as emotionally credible evidence for a false accusation. Vilen old town and an untraceable street The Nameless Street is an urban myth in the old town of central Vilen. Under unknown conditions, a lost visitor may enter it alone. Its buildings and routes form a labyrinth that does not obey the surrounding city. The warning attached to the myth is not to follow anyone encountered there, because those who do may never return to ordinary streets. Days before Fionn's murder, Lynleit is walking with Felix after a work lunch when she abruptly finds herself alone, dizzy, unsteady, and suffering a severe headache. A little girl carrying a red balloon appears, loses it, and runs away crying. Lynleit catches the balloon by its thread and follows the girl's cries so she can return it. The girl eventually stands beside a broken fence above an abrupt drop, looking down at the body of a dead boy. Lynleit releases the balloon in shock. The girl smiles and pushes her from the ledge. Before reaching the ground, Lynleit wakes on a bench in the ordinary city center while Felix fans her face with a piece of paper after her apparent faint. Whether the street is a place, an illusion, or another kind of Holumn remains unresolved. When Lynleit later sees Fionn's body below the hill at the family house, the memory of the boy stupefies her and gives Helena leverage to accuse her of pushing Fionn. Because Lynleit perceives no threshold and Felix witnesses only a faint, the reader must infer whether the street is a physical place, an imposed event, or an experience confined to her consciousness. inferred Felix does not explain why he accepts Lynleit's implausible account without laughing, leaving his response to be read through their long friendship. inferred What conditions admit a visitor to the Nameless Street, and why does it take Lynleit on this day? Are the girl and boy inhabitants, repeated roles, former victims, or images produced by the street? Does the fall release Lynleit, or does another interruption return her to the bench? Does the street anticipate Fionn's death, draw from Lynleit's future, or leave a pattern that later events happen to reactivate? What does Felix observe between Lynleit's last ordinary step and her collapse? Lynleit is already watching Helena study her family, but Fionn remains alive and the danger has not yet broken into an open accusation. Several days later Fionn is found below the hill at the Vilen family house. Lynleit's involuntary recognition of the dead boy gives Helena a true emotional reaction that can be assigned a false cause. Lynleit lynleit Felix felix Fionn fionn Helena helena

entries.title: The Secret Third Ally
entries.subtitle: MOM-008 · The Hidden Wager
entries.text: The Secret Third Ally MOM-008 · The Hidden Wager Lynleit eventually tells only Felix and Reiner that she has recruited Kyrien as an unknown ally and possible trump card against Helena, keeping the decision hidden even from Fionn. Defines Lynleit's first deeply anti-protocol MSF decision early in the story, turns secrecy into an advantage over Helena, and establishes the split between Reiner's trust in Lynleit's judgment and Felix's lasting distrust of Kyrien. Unspecified location Helena knows everyone already inside Lynleit's circle, so an unknown ally creates a favorable information imbalance. Felix and Reiner are already Lynleit's close, long-standing friends before the story begins, not subordinates who become her friends during this crisis. Lynleit eventually confines Kyrien's recruitment to Felix and Reiner and does not inform even Fionn. This is Lynleit's first deeply anti-protocol MSF decision, made with strong intuitive conviction. Fionn's assassination is still far ahead when the compartment is created. The later assassination validates Lynleit's sense of approaching danger, although it does not prove she foresaw the event itself. Felix and Reiner both regard Kyrien as a possible threat to Lynleit, especially when neither bodyguard is near her. Reiner accepts the arrangement because he chooses to trust Lynleit's judgment. Felix accepts only after Reiner's decision leaves him in the minority. Felix never fully learns to trust Kyrien and later clashes with him repeatedly. Lynleit reprimands Felix when those clashes interfere with her decision or the arrangement around Kyrien. Where and when does Lynleit disclose the compartment to Felix and Reiner? What evidence or argument does Lynleit use to justify trusting Kyrien? What continuing cover story protects the compartment from Fionn, Helena, the police, and the wider MSF? Which clash between Felix and Kyrien produces the most serious consequence for Lynleit or an operation? What would Fionn do if he learned Lynleit had hidden Kyrien from him? Lynleit has already coerced Kyrien into service after the failed assassination attempt, but the arrangement initially exists only between handler and asset. Reiner becomes the stabilizing vote that permits the compartment to continue. Felix complies without trust, creating recurring friction with Kyrien and forcing Lynleit to defend the judgment on which the entire imbalance depends. Lynleit lynleit Kyrien kyrien Felix felix Reiner reiner

entries.title: The Unresolved Assassination
entries.subtitle: MOM-007 · The Takeover
entries.text: The Unresolved Assassination MOM-007 · The Takeover Fionn is found dead below the hill at the Vilen family house after several incompatible agendas converge without one actor controlling the whole outcome. Helena knowingly opens one part of the path, then uses his death and Lynleit's stunned response to seize MSF and frame her. Fionn's death connects the hidden conflict to Helena's visible takeover. The unresolved conspiracy contains several motives, partial knowledge, and accidental cooperation, with no single clean chain of command. The hillside grounds of the Vilen family house Fionn is successfully assassinated. His body is found below the hill at the Vilen family house, but whether the fall kills him, follows another attack, or is staged remains unresolved. Lynleit's recent memory of the dead boy on the Nameless Street stupefies her when she sees Fionn below the hill. Helena assigns a false meaning to Lynleit's genuine shock and accuses her of pushing Fionn. His death creates the opening Helena uses to take control of MSF. Helena frames Lynleit for the assassination and directs a hunt for her arrest. Helena knowingly enables one part of the pressure against Fionn without understanding everything that follows. No single participant controls the complete assassination outcome. Several incompatible agendas accidentally cooperate to produce Fionn's death. The broader conflict already includes pressure from criminal Magi, foreign Magiarchates, and church actors. The unresolved issue is how each participant's intended outcome and partial action converge into the assassination. What outcome do the criminal Magi seek around Fionn? What separate outcome does a rival foreign Magiarchate seek? What separate outcome does a church faction seek? Which actions accidentally cooperate even though their authors do not share one objective? Did one faction covertly or illegally infiltrate another and use its people or resources without authorization? Does any participant's apparent affiliation conceal who truly directed them? Which door does Helena knowingly open, what does she expect to happen, and what follows beyond her knowledge? Does the fall kill Fionn, conceal another cause of death, or stage the physical evidence used against Lynleit? Manufactured political strife isolates Fionn and divides his attention while the Spill develops. Days earlier, the Nameless Street gives Lynleit an unexplained memory of a boy lying dead below a fall. Helena converts the vacancy into control of MSF, makes Lynleit the official suspect, and directs a hunt for her arrest while the true authorship remains hidden. Fionn fionn Helena helena

entries.title: The Warning Dismissed
entries.subtitle: MOM-004 · Unknowing Convergence
entries.text: The Warning Dismissed MOM-004 · Unknowing Convergence State Councillor Drake becomes convinced that a coup is developing somewhere inside Narvea, but neither his peers nor the Duke believe he has found more than disconnected irregularities. Establishes the political explanation that first draws government figures toward the disappearances. Court resentment over Drake's friendship with the Duke deepens his isolation until an illegal alliance feels necessary. Ducal Court Drake is deeply convinced that a coup is underway. Drake holds the rank of State Councillor and has an unusually close personal relationship with the Duke. Their friendship begins when Drake is the only official willing to tell the Duke that the Duke is wrong. The Duke openly refers to Drake as a close friend and sometimes forgives his mistakes. Courtiers shun Drake as the Duke's pampered favorite and overlook that he originally earned the relationship by refusing to flatter him. He cannot yet identify where the conspiracy begins or how far it reaches. His peers ridicule the suspicion and the Duke remains skeptical. Drake interprets the park disappearances as possible cover for the illegal movement of material intended for action against Narvea or Ducal authority. The mismatch between Drake's political evidence and the park's impossible events lets the reader infer that the apparent coup is a mask over a deeper conflict involving Fionn, foreign Magiarchs, and church actors. inferred What first convinces Drake that the irregularities form a coup attempt? Which peers lead the ridicule at Court? Is somebody deliberately encouraging the Court to dismiss him? Which criminal Magi, foreign Magiarchates, and church actors are shaping the conspiracy from outside Drake's field of view? Early disappearances and irregular movements need to produce the evidence that Drake reads as one political pattern. Sherie responds to her uncle's isolation by proposing contact with Lynleit outside every lawful chain of supervision. Drake drake

entries.title: Ren L17 “Sparrow”
entries.subtitle: Compact institutional and concealed-carry sidearm
entries.text: Ren L17 “Sparrow” Compact institutional and concealed-carry sidearm Ren L17 Sparrow 9×17 mm / .380 ACP Compact institutional and concealed-carry sidearm Small, discreet, elegant institutional pistol Standard-issued pistol for every MSF officer who has passed weapons certification. MSF purchases the Sparrow from Ren Arms and does not manufacture firearms. A slim, compact, silver-finished pistol with an elegant and deliberately understated appearance. Its proportions sit conceptually between the Walther PPK and SIG Sauer P230, slightly more elongated and graceful than a PPK while retaining enough visual weight to avoid looking fragile. Narrow silver slide Gently rounded upper profile Exposed hammer and small conventional sights Dark grip panels contrasting with silver metal Smooth exterior surfaces and restrained controls Designed for personnel who carry it far more often than they fire it Despite the Sparrow's older design lineage, current-production models omit an external manual safety to reflect the demands and handling priorities of modern combat. The silver finish is standard to the firearm and is not an MSF customization. Routine issue gradually makes the ordinary Ren Arms product visually associated with MSF officers. Its small size, light visual presence, discretion, and modest chambering. lynleit Lynleit Carries the issued Sparrow as her personal sidearm. Walther PPK SIG Sauer P230 Ren Arms Rennel, Narvea

entries.title: Ren L19 “Magpie”
entries.subtitle: Heavier compact service pistol
entries.text: Ren L19 “Magpie” Heavier compact service pistol Ren L19 Magpie 9×19 mm Heavier compact service pistol Larger, louder, and heavier relative of the Sparrow An enlarged and strengthened development of the Sparrow for the more powerful 9×19 cartridge. It retains the older Ren Arms family line while becoming thicker, heavier, visually denser, and more assertive. Graceful slide profile and exposed hammer Narrow forward profile Restrained controls Recognizably Ren Arms grip and frame lines Metallic finishes remain common Darker service finishes may exist Despite the Magpie's older design lineage, current-production models omit an external manual safety to reflect the demands and handling priorities of modern combat. Two optional attachments help the compact pistol remain controllable under the stronger recoil of its 9×19 cartridge. Attachable compensator Reduces muzzle rise and helps the shooter maintain control under the Magpie's greater recoil. Extended magazine Adds gripping surface for firmer recoil control while also increasing ammunition capacity. It fills the space between a discreet institutional pistol and a full modern duty handgun. Its close relationship to the Sparrow, with a larger, louder, heavier, and more noticeable character. SIG Sauer P230 aesthetic lineage SIG Sauer P225 / P239-type proportions Compact CZ influence Ren Arms Rennel, Narvea

entries.title: Ren L22 “Rook”
entries.subtitle: Micro-compact concealed-carry and close-protection pistol
entries.text: Ren L22 “Rook” Micro-compact concealed-carry and close-protection pistol Ren L22 Rook 9×19 mm Micro-compact concealed-carry and close-protection pistol Micro-compact modern carry pistol The Rook moves Ren Arms into a micro-compact service philosophy. It is shorter, slimmer, and more carry-focused than the Sparrow and Magpie while retaining enough grip and slide length to remain credible for trained close-protection and institutional users. Polymer or polymer-dominant frame Slim micro-compact proportions Extended micro-compact grip profile Clean, practical slide surfaces Carry-focused controls and serrations Modern styling without excessive decorative machining Ghost Comp is the Rook's compensated premium configuration, occupying the same conceptual place that a Spectre Comp-style model holds within a micro-compact family. The smallest modern service-oriented member of the family, intended for discreet carry without returning to the older metal-pistol language. A compact, practical, intelligent bird with more confidence and modern utility than a Sparrow. Walther P22Q SIG Sauer P365 XL SIG Sauer P365 Spectre Comp Ren Arms Rennel, Narvea

entries.title: Holumns
entries.subtitle: Manifestations, effects, and evidence
entries.text: Holumns Manifestations, effects, and evidence Holumn is a category of manifestation, not a biological species. A Holumn may be a physical creature, a natural phenomenon, a repeating event, a disembodied will, or a curse. Its shape follows the fear, memory, fixation, or psychic fracture that gives it pressure. No universal weakness exists. A useful countermeasure must answer the rule expressed by the manifestation. An incident may reveal an effect without revealing the whole Holumn behind it. embodied Embodied A creature or body that occupies physical space, including forms that move without being alive. HI-003 HI-004 environmental Environmental Weather, water, terrain, or another natural system becomes the body or behavior of the manifestation. HI-003 HI-004 HI-005 event Event-bound The Holumn exists as a sequence, compulsion, rule, or occurrence with no creature that can be confronted directly. HI-002 HI-005 disembodied Disembodied A voice, memory, desire, or will acquires agency without a stable body of its own. HI-001 curse Curse-bound A person, object, place, or action carries a hostile rule that persists until its particular condition is interrupted. HI-001 HI-002 HI-005

entries.title: MSF
entries.text: MSF # msf Institutional record Known facts only World / MSF MSF Private intelligence contractor One agency, two purposes MSF is a fully private intelligence business that sells its services to the government. The initials are used publicly without a formal expansion. Fionn built a second purpose beneath its contracted work, preparing mostly ordinary people to approach threats they were never told existed. Legal status Fully private business Primary client Narvean government Headquarters Turon Full name Deliberately unrevealed 01 Dual mandate What members see depends on where they stand CONTRACTED FUNCTION Government services MSF sells intelligence, investigation, security, and operational services to the government while remaining institutionally private. FOUNDER'S DESIGN Contingency structure Fionn quietly shaped MSF so it could confront magical crises. Most members were not told that this purpose, or magic itself, existed. PERMANENT CONVERGENCE Two threat domains The Spill is never fully contained. MSF must shrink into a mainly Magi-focused task force while continuing to handle the ordinary intelligence threats it was created to confront. Father Mikhail's discovery that Lynleit has disclosed magic to Kyrien, Felix, and Reiner forces the first institutional answer to knowledge already shared. Lynleit refuses to surrender the three witnesses and instead begins moving MSF toward a partly Magi private enterprise accountable to the Magiarchy and the Church. Open the turning point → See the Church record → 02 Ownership and control The government buys access, not ownership PRIVATE GOVERNANCE Its client cannot run the company The government can negotiate contracts, purchase defined services, and decide whether to keep buying them. It has little authority over MSF's succession, command culture, internal appointments, or ordinary workings beyond the access MSF chooses to permit. MSF may also accept clients beyond the government, exposing the danger of a private contract whose obligations conflict with Narvea's interests. Government power Contract, payment, and requested scope MSF control Clients, succession, personnel, command, and internal rules POLITICAL NICKNAME “A legal mafia.” Politically savvy citizens use the joke because MSF combines private loyalty, public contracts, internal succession, and enough concentrated force to make the state uneasy, all while operating within the law. RESIDENTIAL NODE The Director's House Fionn's family residence also supports selected MSF work through its offices and library, while the formal headquarters remains in Turon. → STANDARD SIDEARM Ren L17 "Sparrow" Every MSF officer who passes weapons certification is issued the compact 9×17 pistol. MSF buys the pistol from Ren Arms and manufactures no weapons. → 03 Cryptology in plain sight Authority is worn in blue MSF · B01 ENCRYPTED M.O. A visible signal that looks ordinary Fionn built cryptology into everyday appearance. A deliberate blue garment initiates recognition, but it does not authenticate authority by itself. Top officers follow it with an innocuous challenge-response hidden inside ordinary conversation. Anyone can buy a blue coat. Only someone trusted by Fionn knows how to answer a question that sounds like small talk. Initiation Blue clothing Verification Conversational challenge-response Audience Top officers trusted by Fionn Origin Fionn's private protocol KNOWN USER Lynleit Her blue coat or jacket initiates Fionn's recognition sequence. Even while she is accused and hunted, she can complete the private exchange known to officers he personally trusted. Open Lynleit's profile → LEGITIMACY FAILURE Helena Fionn's most conservative old officers notice Helena's ignorance first. The people least inclined toward rebellion begin questioning her because strict obedience to the founder's protocol now requires disobedience toward his official successor. Open Helena's profile → 04 Command succession Fionn protects every heir by naming none MSF is a private family enterprise, and its leaders settle succession internally. Fionn deliberately refuses to identify one uncontested successor because he believes a declared heir would become an obvious target. His death divides the inheritance: Lynleit eventually becomes the new Magiarch, while Kyrien inherits the MSF director's seat during her absence. The government has little standing to settle the vacancy, and Fionn's security measure produces the succession crisis it was intended to prevent. 01 Fionn Founder without a declared heir Distributes trust through private protocols and overlapping circles, but refuses to turn any one candidate into a visible target. 02 Helena Contested inheritance Takes control after Fionn's elimination and frames Lynleit for his death. Her ignorance of his private authority protocol gradually gives influential officers reason to doubt the legitimacy of her succession. 03 Lynleit Restoration and contraction Fights to clear her name and reclaim the agency. Because the Spill cannot be fully contained, she reshapes MSF into a smaller task force centered on Magi while preserving its intelligence function. 04 Kyrien Non-Magus director in the Magiarch's absence Inherits control while Lynleit carries the Magiarchate. He must keep a private company, its government contracts, and its permanent Spill mandate functioning without magical authority or the founder's declared succession. 05 Political footprint MSF's concentration of force in Turon MSF's concentration of officers in Turon is sufficient to make a small rebellion or secession imaginable. Officer culture, divided logistics, constitutional loyalty, and the absence of any desire to rebel keep that capacity dormant. Politicians remain uneasy because the state cannot simply command or reorganize its private contractor. The final safeguard is the belief that MSF officers are decent people. See Turon in The Duchy → 06 Operational pairing A knight opens angles. A rook holds the line. ♞ KNIGHT PATTERN Felix Hacking and communications let Felix move through an operation indirectly. He finds unexpected access, redirects information, and reaches positions that a straightforward approach cannot. Open Felix's profile → ♜ ROOK PATTERN Reiner Reiner is the physically imposing brute-force specialist. He anchors protection, takes the direct route, and provides controlled power when a line must be held or broken. Open Reiner's profile → 07 Known personnel People who define the institution Founder Fionn Heir and director Lynleit Successor and rival Helena Unofficial asset, later director Kyrien Hacking and communications Felix Brute force and protection Reiner ✎ Page notes MSF Use notes to refine the agency without turning open questions into canon.
